beats.text: Five lines from books that quietly rearrange how you see things.
"We are such stuff as dreams are made on." — Shakespeare, The Tempest.
"There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so." — Hamlet.
"I am no bird; and no net ensnares me: I am a free human being." — Jane Eyre.
"Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful." — Frankenstein.
"It is a truth universally acknowledged..." — Austen, teaching us to read people, not just rooms.
One sentence can outlast its author by centuries. Which of these stays with you?
